attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, given as his view (he says he is 'no fan of Amodei').

semantics.note: The proposition correctly separates out the safety-pledge part of the sentence and leaves the writers allegation aside. It is a plain past-tense observation about Anthropic.

contract.note: Reading 'core safety pledge' as the RSP's safeguards-before-scaling commitment is the ordinary, informed reading. Using February 2026 for 'recently' is reasonable for a Feb 28 post. Treating a material narrowing as a walk-back, without requiring every commitment to be dropped, is fair.

evidence.note: RSP v2.2 (May 2025) is the baseline. It contains a firm pledge to pause training until ASL-3 security is in place. It sets up the comparison but predates the target period.

Anthropic's Feb 24, 2026 announcement restructures the RSP toward 'more realistic' unilateral commitments and makes the roadmap goals nonbinding rather than hard commitments. This is a dated weakening inside the window.

RSP v3.0 (Feb 24, 2026) keeps commitments to delay development, but only in specific competitor or lead scenarios, and calls them limited. This shows not all obligations were dropped, but it is consistent with the earlier pause pledge being narrowed.

reviews.rationale: On Feb 24, 2026, inside the target window, Anthropic replaced RSP v2.2's firm safeguards-before-scaling pause pledge with v3.0. Version 3.0 makes the roadmap goals nonbinding and limits delay commitments to particular competitor scenarios. That meets the support condition: a central requirement was narrowed or made nonbinding. The commitments v3.0 kept do not show the pledge stayed substantively intact.
